lines: Before your first ride, one question: what should other riders call you?
A new account is asked straight after its code. Continue waits for a name, then you go on to the screen you asked for.
Two to twenty-four letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes or underscores. Anything else is refused, and the field says what's allowed.
The backend holds the one rule. It trims the name and keeps it, or refuses it and leaves the old name as it was.
Profile's headline uses your name, at level one until XP arrives.
Change it from Settings: a dialog opens with your name, and Save updates the headline. Cancel or Escape changes nothing.
Phone to desktop, one calm question, and the dialog becomes a sheet.
What the tests prove: no one rides without a name, a bad one is never kept, and a new one shows at once.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
